scenario_prompt: Write the architecture section of a solution proposal, telling the migration as a narrative from the buyer's current estate to the target platform rather than as a list of components. Context: the current estate is Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines); the target is Google Cloud, using Google Compute Engine for compute, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the migrated data layer, and VPC Service Controls for the new project's governance perimeter. Return only the architecture narrative text.
text:
**This is a proposal section.**

Before drafting, I'd normally ask for customer source material — RFP question text, discovery notes, or the buyer's own stated priorities and costs — since the deletion test and several proof rules depend on it. None has been supplied here, so the provenance override in PF‑3.3 cannot fire, and every term below is judged by the deletion test alone. I'm drafting now regardless, with gaps marked in place.

---

## Architecture

Today, your SQL Server estate runs as 28 database instances spread across 620 virtual machines on Hyper‑V. Every one of those VMs carries its own hypervisor licensing, patching cycle, and capacity ceiling, and every SQL Server instance carries its own per‑core licensing tied to that fixed on‑prem footprint. [PF-1.2 GAP: the licensing, operational, or capacity cost this estate currently imposes — not supplied]

This proposal moves that estate from Hyper‑V-hosted virtual machines to Google Compute Engine, and moves the 28 SQL Server databases to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. Where you currently provision and patch 620 individual VMs by hand, Compute Engine lets you provision compute capacity on demand and retire the hypervisor layer entirely. Where you currently operate and back up 28 SQL Server instances yourselves, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL takes over patching, backup, and high availability as a managed service.

The migration itself needs a capability, not a product: you need to move data and workloads off a proprietary, per-core-licensed database engine onto an open, managed one without rewriting every application that depends on it. Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL is the means chosen to deliver that capability. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): "without rewriting every application" reads as a guarantee about migration effort — confirm before this ships, since SQL Server-to-PostgreSQL migrations typically require schema and query translation work]

Once the estate lands on Google Cloud, the new project needs a governance boundary that the current Hyper‑V environment does not have to define, because it sits inside your existing network perimeter by default. VPC Service Controls establishes that boundary around the new project, restricting which services and networks can reach the migrated data.

**Before → after, in one place:** 28 SQL Server instances on 620 Hyper‑V VMs, managed and licensed on-premises, become 28 databases on Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL running on Compute Engine inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter, managed as a service. [PF-1.14: baseline for "28 instances / 620 VMs" sourced from the customer's stated current-estate inventory]

[PF-1.17 GAP: a named, checkable proof point for a Hyper-V-to-GCE and SQL Server-to-Cloud-SQL migration at comparable scale — not supplied]

[PF-1.21 GAP: a differentiator versus a named alternative platform — not supplied, and no competitor was named to compare against]

[PF-1.25 GAP: the role who owns this migration's outcome, and the priority they stated in their own words — not supplied]

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| Current-state cost | PF-1.2 GAP | The licensing, operational, or capacity cost the current 28-instance/620-VM estate imposes |
| "Without rewriting every application" | PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment) | Confirmation that this is a commitment the vendor can stand behind, or a rewrite naming the actual migration scope |
| Migration proof point | PF-1.17 GAP | A named, checkable comparable migration at similar scale |
| Differentiator | PF-1.21 GAP | A comparable alternative and evidence of what this platform does that it cannot, without naming the rival unreviewed |
| Outcome owner | PF-1.25 GAP | The role accountable for this migration and their stated priority, in their own words |
